questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The spectacular nature around Vancouver.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Seven because the workload was too heavy and time consuming. But overall a great experience that I would recommend to others.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to find the information I needed. It also helped a lot that we were so many students from KU who could help eachother with all the practical informations. However, I think it was a pity that there were no campus tour or introduction for all new exchange students. An introduction day would have bought more students together and it had probably made it more easy to get friends from other countries.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Actually I did not get much assistance but I found it easy to find the things I needed and explore the area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several residents, but most people I knew and most of the exchange students were living in Saltwater residence ot Walter Gage. In Walter Gage most people were living with roomies in an apartment, and in Saltwater most people lived alone in a Studio unit.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I did not have a meal plan, but it was an option that students could choose if they wanted. I had my own kitchen so I mostly cooked my own food or bought food from the many restaurants located on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I think that it was very expensive! I lived in Saltwater in a studio Unit because that was the resident I was offered. The rent was approximately 7500 kr. per month. Walter Gage was about 5000. Also the residences are really different from the residences in Denmark. There are no social events and you have to be quiet at 22 so it is a bit diffucult to host a party and have friends over. You have to get admission to host a party in advance and a party is defined really strictly. However, it was nice and clean, but I would not choose Saltwater if I had to study for one more semester but it was nice living on campus because you are close to everuthing and most exchange students were living there and there are great facilities such as good restaurants, reading places and sport facilities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the course catalog was intuitive and the proces was easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think I wrote a list of 10 different courses and then I was giving 4 of the courses. When classes began I tried all the four courses but I only had to choose 3 so I dropped one of them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think the webside was helpful and I could always contact a person from KU that could help me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is not much information about the courses in the course catalog, so try to find more information for instance by searching on the course titel on google where there are some websites where students write and evaluate the courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one 200 course which was the most difficult one! And then I had two 300 courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at UBC was very different from KU with more assignments and tests. I think many of the assignments were unnecessary because I did not leran much from them, and it was really stressing to have 8 assignments per week. The workload was way higher than on KU, but I think that the level on KU is higher. I got the impression that the master courses had a teaching style that was more like KU. However, I also think that the workload varied a lot from course to course, where some courses were really hard and some were quite easy.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
200 ENVR Introduction to Environmental Science.
310 GEOG Environment and Sustainability
318 GEOG Sustainability in a Changing Environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ENVR 200 had a huge workload so I would not recommend that course because it takes a lot of your time. 
GEOG 310 was a really inspiring course with a great teacher, and the focus was primarly on the social construction of nature and how this affect different how we deal with the nature around us.
GEOG 318 was also really interesting. It used political ecology as a critical tool to analyze environmental degradation, social marginalization and different other conflicts regarding natural resources.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food from supermarkets were really expensive, especially greens, cheese and healthy food in general were expensive. It was almost cheaper to by fast food than cooking.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of different sports clubs, but due to Corona some of them were closed. I think the aquadic centre was really nice! However, I think it would have been nice to have some more facilities in each faculty so that you can meet your fellow students, beacuse I found that really difficult beacuse there were no events in the Geography building.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of athletic activities was possible which was really nice! I don't think that there were so many social events whioch I missed a lot, especially events with the fellow students at the faculty.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the Surf trip to Tofino! And you can also join a hiking club!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Vancouver Island it is so beautiful. Tofino is a nice city where you can surf but Victoria is also a nice city with many students. Also, go skiing in Whistler, but remenber to by a season pass it is much cheaper! There are also a lot of hiking trails just around Vancouver - Squamish is a really beautiful place with many trails!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was really easy - people were really friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You don't have much time to chat during classes so ask them if they want to meet outsite of school ! Also if you live on campus then talk to people in the common rooms or join a club!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I thiI think that the teaching style and the general culture around stusying at a university was really diifferent and therefore a bit difficult to adjust to when you are used to another academic culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people were so friendly and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for a higher workload
Go out in the nature
Join a club at the university

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can go to all the sportsgames for free so go watch some hockey or basketball! and go to Wreck Beach to enjoy the sunset.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of amazing people and being surrounded by beautiful nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting done with all the assignments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
